issues.legal_issue: A requirement that an administrative land-acquisition award receive prior government approval is constitutionally valid when the award is an offer made by a government agent rather than a judicial determination.
material_facts: The Deputy Commissioner was required to determine the area, compensation, and apportionment in an acquisition award, but could not make the award without prior government approval.
The court characterized the award as an offer of compensation and the Deputy Commissioner as acting administratively as the Government’s agent, not in a judicial or quasi-judicial capacity.
The statutory scheme allowed an interested person who did not accept the award to seek a court determination of compensation, with compensation governed by statutory criteria.
issues.conclusion: The prior-approval requirement did not violate Article 31(2) of the Constitution; the Deputy Commissioner’s authority was subject to government approval because the award was an administrative offer made on behalf of the Government.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Article 31(2) and noted that the Land Acquisition Act was protected under Article 31(5). An award under section 11 was an offer of compensation, not a judicial or quasi-judicial decision, and the Deputy Commissioner acted as an agent of the Government. Sections 15, 18, 23, 24, and 26 provided for statutory compensation criteria and a court determination when an interested person did not accept the award. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and award_is_administrative_offer and award_maker_acts_as_government_agent and award_maker_lacks_judicial_role

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the acquisition of land and compensation for that acquisition.
predicates.award_is_administrative_offer: The award-maker determines proposed compensation as an offer rather than as a final judicial determination.
predicates.award_maker_acts_as_government_agent: The award-maker performs the award function on behalf of the government.
predicates.award_maker_lacks_judicial_role: The award-maker acts administratively and does not exercise a judicial or quasi-judicial function.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition proceeding involves an administrative compensation offer made by a government agent who has no judicial role, prior government approval of that offer is constitutionally valid.

issues.legal_issue: The requirement of prior government approval for a land-acquisition award has adequate governing standards when the government must apply the statutory compensation framework and compensation disputes can be referred to a court.
material_facts: The Government had to take the Act’s provisions into account when approving an award.
The statutory framework directed the compensation assessment to specified criteria and allowed an interested person who did not accept the award to seek a court determination.
The Court held that grievances about the amount of compensation or other compensation-related matters could be remedied under the Act.
issues.conclusion: The contention that there were no guidelines for government approval was erroneous; the governing statutory framework supplied the applicable standards and remedies.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on sections 15, 18, 23, 24, and 26 of the Mysore Land Acquisition Act. The Government had to consider the Act’s provisions; the compensation criteria applied to the Collector’s assessment and the court’s determination, and an interested person could seek a court reference if the award was not accepted. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the acquisition of land and compensation for that acquisition.
predicates.government_approval_is_governed_by_compe: The government must assess the award under the applicable legal framework for determining compensation.
predicates.compensation_can_be_referred_for_court_d: A person who does not accept the award can obtain a court determination of compensation.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition proceeding requires government approval under the compensation framework and an unaccepted compensation award can be referred to a court, the approval has adequate guiding standards.
